result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide, multi-lane arterial road with significant pavement degradation and a lack of marked crossings for the primary direction of travel. While a marked crosswalk and curb ramp are present for the side street, the overall design prioritizes vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety and connectivity.

hazards.name: Missing Crosswalk
hazards.description: No marked crossing is provided across the main arterial road, forcing pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without guidance.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Significant cracking and uneven surfaces in the roadway create tripping hazards and may affect vehicle braking performance.

hazards.name: Long Unprotected Crossing
hazards.description: The width of the main road creates a long exposure time for pedestrians without a median refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main road at the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility zebra-style crosswalks across all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement bulb-outs at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features well-maintained sidewalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps, but lacks critical safety infrastructure for crossing. Despite being a signalized intersection in a residential area, there are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals, creating significant ambiguity and risk for people on foot.

hazards.name: Unmarked crossing
hazards.description: The absence of painted crosswalks at a signalized intersection reduces pedestrian visibility and fails to define a safe crossing path.

hazards.name: Missing pedestrian signals
hazards.description: Lack of dedicated pedestrian signal heads forces users to rely on vehicle signals, which may not provide sufficient crossing time.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalk markings
interventions.description: Install continental or zebra-style markings to clearly delineate the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian countdown signals
interventions.description: Install signal heads with countdown timers to improve predictability and safety for crossing pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image depicts a two-lane roadway with a high-visibility continental crosswalk and a sidewalk on the left side. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps is present, the lack of a continuous sidewalk network on both sides and the absence of pedestrian-specific signals or signage at the crossing point reduce overall safety.

hazards.name: Discontinuous Sidewalk Network
hazards.description: The sidewalk is only present on one side of the street, forcing pedestrians to walk on the grass or in the roadway on the opposite side.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks pedestrian-actuated signals or warning signage to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Visible cracking and wear in the asphalt near the crosswalk could present a tripping hazard or affect vehicle braking.
hazards.location_in_image: Road surface within and adjacent to the crosswalk

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a paved sidewalk on the right side of the road to provide a continuous and safe path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-actuated flashing beacons to increase driver awareness and yielding rates at the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve the visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with marked zebra crosswalks and pedestrian signals, providing basic infrastructure for crossing. However, the environment is characterized by wide roadways, significant crossing distances, and a lack of continuous, high-quality sidewalk networks, which are typical of commercial and industrial areas.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic in a single stage without the protection of a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: The wide crosswalk spanning the main roadway in the foreground.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Visible cracking and wear on the road surface within the intersection area.
hazards.location_in_image: Road surface throughout the intersection and near the crosswalks.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised refuge island in the center of the wide roadway to reduce exposure time and allow for two-stage crossing.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Connectivity Improvements
interventions.description: Extend and widen the sidewalk network to ensure a continuous and accessible path for pedestrians throughout the commercial zone.
